PC-metadata correlation plot of a PCAtools pca object

Source: R/pcaPlots.R
pcaEigencorPlot.Rd

The interactive counterpart of PCAtools::eigencorplot(): the correlation of each component's sample scores with each metadata variable, as a heatmap with the coefficient and its significance in every cell. Non-numeric metadata are converted to integer codes (factor level order), as PCAtools requires numeric variables; their labels say so.

Usage

pcaEigencorPlot(
  pcaobj,
  components = NULL,
  metavars = NULL,
  cor.method = "pearson",
  p.adjust.method = "none",
  plot.rsquared = FALSE,
  low.color = "#00008B",
  mid.color = "#FFFFFF",
  high.color = "#8B0000",
  show.values = TRUE,
  digits = 2,
  main = NULL
)

Arguments

pcaobj

A PCAtools pca object.

components

Components to correlate, by name. Default: the first 10.

metavars

Metadata columns to correlate. Default: all of them.

cor.method

"pearson", "spearman" or "kendall".

p.adjust.method

A stats::p.adjust() method, applied across every cell.

plot.rsquared

Logical; show R-squared instead of the signed coefficient.

low.color, mid.color, high.color

Colour scale. For R-squared, the scale runs from mid.color to high.color.

show.values

Logical; print the value and significance stars in each cell.

digits

Decimal places of the printed values.

main

Optional plot title.

Value

A plotly object, with the long correlation table (coefficient, p-value, adjusted p-value) as attribute "table".

See also

pcaEigencorPlotServer(), PCAtools::eigencorplot()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

data(example_pca)
pcaEigencorPlot(example_pca, components = paste0("PC", 1:5))
